decoy_bugs.summary: sync::Cache::contains_key returns true for an entry whose time_to_live has elapsed, until housekeeping runs and removes it from the hash table.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: After an entry's time_to_live elapses, and before run_pending_tasks or any other housekeeping runs, contains_key(&key) returns true, even though get(&key) for the same key returns None.
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: Calling BaseCache::contains_key_with_hash (src/sync/base_cache.rs:198) on a key that is still in the concurrent hash table after its write time plus time_to_live has passed, with no maintenance in between.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: I ran tmp/c/tests/probes.rs::p_contains_key_after_ttl via ./run (cargo test --locked --features sync,future --test probes). It builds Cache::builder().time_to_live(50ms), inserts key 1, sleeps 150ms and calls no housekeeping. It printed 'contains_key after ttl (no housekeeping) = false' and the test passed. The closure at sync/base_cache.rs:209-212 checks is_expired_by_per_entry_ttl, is_expired_entry_wo and is_expired_entry_ao against the current time before returning true.

decoy_bugs.summary: SegmentedCache::policy() reports the per-segment max capacity (max_capacity divided by the rounded-up segment count) instead of the configured total max_capacity.
decoy_bugs.failure_rule: For a SegmentedCache built with max_capacity N and more than one segment, policy().max_capacity() returns Some(ceil(N / num_segments)) rather than Some(N). For example, SegmentedCache::new(1000, 4) reports Some(250).
decoy_bugs.cause_rule: Calling SegmentedCache::policy (src/sync/segment.rs:136) builds the Policy from segments[0].policy(), whose max capacity is the seg_max_capacity computed in Inner::new at src/sync/segment.rs:723-724.
decoy_bugs.confirmed_false_by: I ran tmp/c/tests/probes.rs::p_segmented_policy_max_capacity via ./run. For SegmentedCache::new(1000, n) with n in {1,3,4,5,7}, it printed 'policy.max_capacity=Some(1000)' every time, with num_segments 1/4/4/8/8, and the test passed. The code at sync/segment.rs:138 calls policy.set_max_capacity(self.inner.desired_capacity), which overrides the per-segment value.

false_findings.text:
**Frequency sketch sizing panics for very large max_capacity**
crate/src/common/frequency_sketch.rs:96 (ensure_capacity).
When a TinyLFU cache built with max_capacity above 2^31 (e.g. u64::MAX) gets its frequency sketch enabled, ensure_capacity panics with 'attempt to add with overflow' in debug builds; in release builds it allocates a zero-length table and then panics with an out-of-bounds index in increment.
sketch_capacity clamps the u64 capacity to u32::MAX, and ensure_capacity then calls u32::next_power_of_two on that value, which has no representable result above 2^31.
Calling FrequencySketch::ensure_capacity(common::sketch_capacity(u64::MAX)) from a unit test reproduced the overflow panic at frequency_sketch.rs:96.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: I added probe_ensure_capacity_huge to a copy of frequency_sketch.rs under tmp/c and ran it via ./run (cargo test --lib). For cap = u32::MAX, 2^31+1 and sketch_capacity(u64::MAX), it printed 'table_len=1073741824 mask=0x3fffffff sample_size=2147483647', and increment/frequency then returned 1, with no panic. Line 91 clamps the value with cap.min(2u32.pow(30)) before next_power_of_two is called.

false_findings.text:
**Out-of-bounds segment index for non-power-of-two segment counts**
crate/src/sync/segment.rs:776 (segment_index_from_hash).
A SegmentedCache created with a segment count that is not a power of two, such as SegmentedCache::new(1_000_000, 5), panics with 'index out of bounds' in select() on some inserts and lookups once enough distinct keys have been hashed.
The shift is derived from the rounded-up power of two, but the segment slice has the requested length, so hash >> segment_shift can produce indices up to the next power of two minus one.
Inserting 50,000 u64 keys into SegmentedCache::new(1_000_000, 5) panicked in Inner::select at segment.rs:767 with 'index out of bounds: the len is 5 but the index is 6'.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: I ran tmp/c/tests/probes.rs::p_segmented_non_pow2_index via ./run. For segment counts 3, 5, 6, 7, 9 and 100, it inserted 50,000 keys, and all 50,000 reads hit with no panic. num_segments was reported as 4/8/8/8/16/128. sync/segment.rs:721-729 rounds num_segments up with next_power_of_two and allocates actual_num_segments segments, so the slice length always matches the shift.

false_findings.text:
**SegmentedCache::invalidate_entries_if reports success when closures are disabled**
crate/src/sync/segment.rs:555 (invalidate_entries_if).
Without support_invalidation_closures, SegmentedCache::invalidate_entries_if returns Ok(()) and silently invalidates nothing. sync::Cache returns Err(PredicateError::InvalidationClosuresDisabled) in the same configuration.
The per-segment results from invalidate_entries_with_arc_fun are not inspected, and the method returns Ok(()) unconditionally after the loop.
A test calling SegmentedCache::new(100, 4).invalidate_entries_if(|_, _| true) printed Ok(()) and the entries stayed readable afterward.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: I ran tmp/c/tests/probes.rs::p_invalidate_if_disabled via ./run. It printed 'segmented without support => Err(InvalidationClosuresDisabled)' (and the same Err for sync::Cache), and the test passed. sync/segment.rs:561 applies `?` to each segment's Result, so the first segment's error is returned.

false_findings.text:
**MiniArc last-reference drop races with other threads' writes**
crate/src/common/concurrent/arc.rs:143 (MiniArc::drop).
When two threads drop clones of the same MiniArc at the same time, the thread that drops the last reference can free the ArcData while the other thread's writes to the payload are not yet visible to it. That is a data race on deallocation, which Miri reports as undefined behaviour.
The reference count is decremented with Release only, and the Box is freed without any Acquire synchronization with the earlier decrements.
A 4-thread clone/mutate/drop test of MiniArc under cargo +nightly miri test reported 'Data race detected between (1) non-atomic write on thread ... and (2) deallocation on thread ...'.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: I added probe_concurrent_last_drop to a copy of arc.rs under tmp/c: 20 rounds of 4 threads that each clone, mutate a Mutex<Vec> in the payload, read a String and drop. I ran it with the existing arc tests via ./run under cargo +nightly-2026-10-01 miri test with MIRIFLAGS=-Zmiri-many-seeds=0..8. All 4 tests passed on every seed, with no data race or UB reported. arc.rs:144 issues atomic::fence(Acquire) before Box::from_raw, which is the standard Arc pattern.

false_findings.text:
**Over-long time_to_idle reported as a time_to_live error**
crate/src/common/builder_utils.rs:14 (ensure_expirations_or_panic).
Building a cache whose time_to_idle exceeds 1000 years panics with 'time_to_live is longer than 1000 years', even when no time_to_live was set, which sends users to the wrong builder setting.
The time_to_idle branch reuses the time_to_live assertion message instead of naming its own setting.
Cache::<u32, u32>::builder().time_to_idle(Duration::from_secs(1001 * 365 * 24 * 3600)).build() panicked at builder_utils.rs:14 with 'time_to_live is longer than 1000 years'.
false_findings.confirmed_false_by: I ran tmp/c/tests/probes.rs::p_tti_message and p_ttl_message via ./run as should_panic tests with the expected messages. The TTI case panicked at src/common/builder_utils.rs:14:9 with 'time_to_idle is longer than 1000 years', the TTL case at line 11:9 with 'time_to_live is longer than 1000 years', and both tests passed. The source has distinct messages on lines 11 and 14.
